prerequisites.title: Kintone admin access
prerequisites.detail: Registering the client and enabling users needs the User & System Administration page.

prerequisites.title: Public HTTPS redirect URL
prerequisites.detail: Kintone requires a redirect endpoint. Copy the redirect URI from the Composio dashboard.

steps.title: Open OAuth settings in Kintone admin
steps.detail: Log in, click the gear icon, open User & System Administration, then OAuth under System Administration.
steps.done_when: The OAuth client list is visible.

steps.title: Copy redirect URI from Composio
steps.detail: Copy the redirect URI from the Composio dashboard for the kintone_rest auth config.

steps.title: Add the OAuth client
steps.detail: Click Add OAuth Client, enter a client name and the redirect endpoint, and save.
steps.done_when: Client ID, client secret and endpoints are shown.

steps.title: Enable users with Configure users
steps.detail: Check the users who may use the client and save. New users are unchecked by default.

steps.title: Create Composio auth config
steps.detail: Create a kintone_rest auth config with your client ID and secret, and request the scopes you need, separated by spaces.
steps.done_when: Auth config exists and a test connection succeeds.

traps.title: Authorization codes are valid for 10 minutes
traps.detail: Authorization codes are valid for 10 minutes.

traps.title: Users are disabled by default
traps.detail: No user can use a new client until an admin checks them in Configure users. Each newly created Kintone user is also unchecked.

traps.title: IP restrictions block OAuth
traps.detail: OAuth client features fail on domains with IP restrictions unless the client's IP is whitelisted.

traps.title: Client limited to its own domain
traps.detail: Access is limited to users in the Kintone domain where the client was registered. Multi-customer use is not documented.

traps.title: Token and client limits
traps.detail: Max 20 OAuth clients, and 10 refresh tokens per client per user. Access tokens last 1 hour; refresh tokens do not expire.

traps.title: Redirect URI must match exactly
traps.detail: The URI in the token request must equal the one in the authorization request, and be URL-encoded.

blockers.symptom: Users cannot complete the OAuth flow
blockers.what_it_means: The user is not enabled for the client in Configure users.
blockers.what_to_do: Have a Kintone admin check the user in Configure users and save.

blockers.symptom: OAuth fails on a domain with IP restrictions
blockers.what_it_means: The client's IP is not whitelisted.
blockers.what_to_do: Ask the admin to whitelist the OAuth client's IP.

open_questions: Can one OAuth client serve users in other customers' Kintone domains, or must each customer register one? Check with Kintone developer support.

items.reason: Quote states the developer clicks the green Add OAuth Client button, i.e. manual registration in admin settings.
Quote says Configure users sets which users in the Kintone domain may interact with the client, limiting access to the domain's users.
Quote says scopes limit token access and do not grant permissions beyond the user's access.
Quote says by default no users can interact with the client until given permission through Configure users.
Quote describes choosing users on the Configure Users screen and clicking save.
Quote says OAuth client features cannot be used from IP-restricted domains unless the client IP is whitelisted.
Quote says a new user's checkbox is unchecked by default and the OAuth client is disabled for them.
Quote states up to 20 OAuth clients can be registered.
Quote states up to 10 refresh tokens can be generated from 1 client for 1 user.
Quote states access tokens are valid for 1 hour.
Quote states refresh tokens do not expire.
Quotes cover registration and admin user configuration, but say nothing explicitly about provider review being unnecessary; the no-review conclusion is only implied.
Quotes describe the two steps in order: add OAuth client in admin settings, then Configure users to enable users.
Quotes state no users can interact by default and the admin must choose users on Configure Users and save.
Quote states IP-restricted domains need the client IP whitelisted before OAuth client features work.

Quotes support the single-domain setup steps but contain no timing (1-2 hours) and nothing about wider multi-customer setups; the time estimate is unsupported and the 'not documented' conclusion is only implied.
